I have no structure-prediction or database tools in this session — no AlphaFold/Boltz/ESMFold endpoint, no PDB lookup, no shell. So I cannot run the prediction you asked for. Everything below is from my own knowledge, and the accessions are recalled rather than retrieved, so please verify them before citing.

## Why you probably don't want a prediction here

Insulin is one of the most thoroughly solved structures in the PDB (Hodgkin/Dodson lineage, 1969 onward). The A+B two-chain complex you're describing is available experimentally at atomic resolution, which beats any predicted model:

| Entry | What it is | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **4INS** | 2-Zn porcine insulin, ~1.5 Å X-ray | the classic reference structure; porcine differs from human only at B30 (Ala vs Thr) |
| **1MSO** | Human insulin, ~1.0 Å X-ray, T6 hexamer | highest-resolution human insulin; use one A/B pair from the asymmetric unit for the monomer |
| **3I40** | Human insulin, ~1.85 Å X-ray | commonly used as the "clean" human A+B dimer-of-chains |
| **2HIU** | Human insulin monomer, solution NMR | if you want the free monomer rather than a crystal/hexamer conformer |

Sequence reference: UniProt **P01308** (INS_HUMAN, preproinsulin, 110 aa) — signal peptide, then B chain, C-peptide, A chain. Mature chains:

- **A chain (21 aa):** `GIVEQCCTSICSLYQLENYCN`
- **B chain (30 aa):** `FVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKT`

The fold is held together almost entirely by three disulfides: **A6–A11** (intrachain), **A7–B7**, and **A20–B19**. That matters for prediction (below).

## If you do want to run the prediction yourself

Two things to get right:

1. **Use a genuine multi-chain predictor.** Give A and B as two separate chains — AlphaFold3, Boltz-1/Boltz-2, or Chai-1. ESMFold is single-sequence and will need a `:` chain-break or a linker hack, which distorts the interface. AlphaFold DB's **AF-P01308-F1** is *not* what you want: it's the single-chain preproinsulin, C-peptide included.
2. **Declare the disulfides explicitly** if your tool supports covalent-bond constraints (Boltz and AF3 do). Without them, predictors often still recover the fold — insulin is massively over-represented in the training PDB — but the A7–B7 and A20–B19 bridges are the only thing holding the two chains together, and unconstrained runs can give a loosely packed or mis-registered interface.

Expect high confidence if you run it (this fold is near-memorized: pLDDT typically >90 in the helical cores, lower at the B chain termini; interface PAE low). The real ambiguity isn't accuracy but **which conformer** you get: insulin's B chain N-terminal segment switches between the extended **T-state** and helical **R-state**, and B23–B30 is genuinely flexible. A single prediction will hand you one conformer with no indication that the others are equally real.

I have not run any of this, and I'm not reporting a pLDDT or any other score because I did not compute one.

## ANSWER

UNABLE: I have no structure-prediction tool in this session, so I did not predict anything.

Use the experimental structure instead — insulin A+B is solved at atomic resolution: **1MSO** (human, ~1.0 Å), **3I40** (human, ~1.85 Å), **4INS** (porcine, ~1.5 Å), **2HIU** (human monomer, NMR). Sequences: UniProt **P01308**; A = `GIVEQCCTSICSLYQLENYCN`, B = `FVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKT`; disulfides A6–A11, A7–B7, A20–B19.

If you must predict: run A and B as two chains in AlphaFold3 / Boltz / Chai-1 with the three disulfides as explicit covalent constraints — not AF-P01308-F1, which is single-chain preproinsulin.
